claim: In the minimum constraint removal problem with line obstacles (not segments), the problem can be solved in linear time by checking whether start and goal are on the same side of each line.
falsifier: One can implement the linear-time algorithm and verify its correctness on instances with line obstacles.

conditions: start and goal points are given
the problem is to find the minimum number of lines to remove
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the reported claim and the specific problem setting; transfer to other obstacle types is unestablished.

title: Obstacle type: lines for linear-time solvability

claim: A quantum prover-verifier verification protocol for an NP-complete problem, in which the verifier receives limited information from an untrusted prover in the form of a series of unentangled quantum states, experimentally demonstrates a quantum computational advantage over classical computation.
falsifier: Re-run the reported verification protocol on the same NP-complete verification task and compare the verifier's completion time and success behavior against the classical baseline under the stated unentangled-state and limited-information conditions.

conditions: computational task is verification of an NP-complete problem
proof is sent as a series of unentangled quantum states
verifier gets only limited information about the proof
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the reported experimental implementation, task, and conditions; transfer beyond them is unestablished.

title: Quantum verification protocol–quantum computational advantage principle
